root_idea.summary: The root is centered on blindness, especially blindness present from birth, with a related extension to obscurity or gloom.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence distinguishes congenital blindness from blindness or loss of an eye arising after an affliction, and also preserves a Classical adjectival use for land enveloped in gloom.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized masculine singular lexical citation form.

senses.definition: Blind from birth; a person born without sight.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the adjective is used substantivally with the definite article, including in the expression for healing the blind-born.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose eye or sight has been lost after birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended Classical use for acquired loss of an eye or sight, distinct from the congenital-blindness sense established for the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of land: enveloped in gloom or obscurity; overcast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description specifically applied to land.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The land adjective meaning is represented under the Classical meaning for كَمْهَاءٌ.

cautions: The Quranic contextual gloss varies between “the blind” and “the born blind,” while the supplied lexical discussion specifically supports blindness from birth.
Lane equates the land adjective with مُغَمَّةٌ and مِغَمَّةٌ but does not supply the referenced غم entry here; “overcast” and “gloomy” are therefore broad renderings of that equivalence.
